contract: Durable Assembly in plain Elixir with no table, process, timer or state of its own that hosts a room as the continuation chain of delivery/durable-mailbox, one assembly/run-engine Run per link on a fresh Unit room/<sha256(tenant NUL chain)>/<seq> with the workflow/turn-policy root pattern and its version pinned in state/recipe-store. open/3 checks the start (check_start/2, link 1, no carry, the reserve) before it pins, opens the chain and starts the first Run, and after a conflicting open, also a repeated one, removes the request's pin for the first Run ID unless that chain's first link holds the same Run and pin. deliver/3 gives one mail input only to an idle tip, refuses mail of the room's own schemas or of a turn-ID form, and settles each message by the engine reply and the classification read after it (record_size stops the link, definite engine refusals are refused, lost replies, exits and halts stay delivering); it gives the rollover message instead when the slot count, request count or clock leaves less than the per-message reserve (B turns of the declared bot worst case with their posts, one notice, and the decision worst case under decided or a host rule) plus the carry and finish. wake/3 routes the host timer and gives a delivering message again before the wake. rollover/3 of the link link_seq returns {:not_tip, seq} with nothing written when the tip is another link, then reads result/3 (a valid finished carry, else restart_carry/1 with the same checks), settles a claimed message from transcript/3, unpins an earlier plan of another version, plans and pins, takes the mailbox's atomic step (a plan_mismatch unpins its own pin), starts the successor and unpins the old Run; resume/3 finishes a stopped sequence. Every call can be repeated with the same request; fixed tagged errors, no retry, log or telemetry.
limits: The room is as sound as its Needs: one deliverer per chain, no control (Attempt change, cancel) during a call, a true declared reserve, a start Need that builds the engine with the room's bindings, schemas and result_reader, a wake timer at each slot deadline and Run deadline, a deadline margin above the longest engine call and the clock difference, and read limits that cover one link's history. It checks none of them.

The slot count as the lifetime action count and the meaning of status classification are readings of assembly/run-engine's code (owner answer Q8); the tests run the real engine, so a change of either fails them.

A refused message reads not shown to have been given: after a lost reply, an outcome landing between the reply and the read, a request without room in control, a lost reply whose message reached the pattern with no turn or decision naming it admitted, or an Attempt change between two calls that makes the re-given input ID conflict (input_id_conflict), a message that a pattern was given can be settled refused; the host decides whether to put it again.
An open/3 that pinned, failed and is never repeated leaves its pin record for the first Run ID, and that version then cannot be deleted; the host repeats open/3 after an error.
No exactly-once delivery: a message is given at most once per Run by the engine's input IDs and to exactly one link by the mailbox.

A tip whose carry does not complete gets no more mail and ends at its Run deadline, then restarts; a stalled turn holds the room until its deadline and a stalled tip until its Run deadline; a rollover at link 2^31-1 is refused (link_limit).
One tenant's recipe-store stream holds 10,000 records and each link appends a pin and an unpin, so one tenant's rooms run out of links at about 5,000 until that stream gains compaction (#821).
Mail payloads and carries hold people's text and have no delete or erasure.
No child Run, parent-close rule, timer, process, A2A peer, live channel or cross-node room; a chain keeps its rule.

The test harness hosts one engine at a time (the run-engine fixture routes the Unit's offers to one name), so a link's record is read before its successor starts; finite listed scenarios, not a proof.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios pass on the worker's disposable PostgreSQL 16 with the real run-engine (fixture/1, one Run per link begun in its Run owner), the real durable mailbox in random schemas as the application role, the real turn-policy step with scripted bots and decisions and the real recipe store on the Memory Store with a log hook, and an engine stand-in for the record_size, indeterminate, exit and halt replies: case 1 turns posted, a message put during a turn busy then given, a 128-byte member; case 2 each check_start reason, link 2, a carry, the reserve at 256 and 257 for actions and requests, a pin error, equal and conflicting opens, a chain created between the read and the open (own pin removed when the pins differ, kept when equal), an equal open after the first rollover; case 3 the request_count and clock edges; case 4 a finished rollover with the carried queue run first and mail to the old Run ID given once to the successor; case 5 restarts at the Run deadline, after a carried queue (restarted_queue_dropped, no turn run again), for a carry naming another link, and a restarted carry over a larger reserve changing nothing; case 7 settlement from the transcript (absent, turn ran, no turn naming it, a transcript error, a result error); case 8 pin deleted, indeterminate, stream_full at 10,000 records, plan review M2 and M3; case 9 a crash before step 1, after steps 3(b), 3, 4, 5 and 6 and after open/3's start Need; case 10 kept and changed versions and a delete refused pinned at three points; case 11 each engine reply and classification, lost replies, an exit, a halt and restart, a record_size lost reply before a wake, a missing schema, two clocks and the refused room schemas; case 12 shapes. Finite scenarios, not a proof.

Listed scenarios at the engine's 256 lifetime actions pass on the real engine: a message delivered at slots + A + 2 = 256 whose turns all fit, the rollover message with one more slot, a decided message just inside the reserve with its decision and picked turns, the rollover message where a reserve without the decision part would admit a message that passes 256, the slot edge on a finished successor on a fresh Unit, and a turn over 256 actions refused invalid_request then ended out_of_time by wakes at the slot and Run deadlines and restarted. Finite scenarios, not a proof.
OTP 29.1.2 crypto:hash(sha256, Data) computes the chain hash of the Run and Unit IDs.
Pinned Elixir GenServer.call/3 exits when the call ends by its limit or the server dies; the room catches that exit of an engine call.

The host runs one deliverer per chain and gives no control during a call, declares the true worst case of its recipes and decision binding, builds each engine through the start Need with the room's bindings, schemas, result_reader and a run_deadline past the margin, wakes the tip at each slot deadline and Run deadline and calls deliver/3 after a wake at the Run deadline, repeats open/3 after an error, rolls over the link that rollover/3 names, reconciles halted engines, and vouches for each mail's from and reply_to_member.

telemetry.contract: The room emits no events and no logs; the engine, mailbox and recipe store keep their own declarations.

config.contract: The binding from new/1 (exactly mailbox, recipes, principal, turn_policy, the start and engine Needs, clock, request_cap 1..256, the reserve and read_limits, else invalid_binding) is the only configuration, fixed for the value's life; no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle of its own: the host owns the engines, their reconciliation and the wake timer.
